newsitem.title: SPAIN: Iraq calls on European Union to help lift embargo.
newsitem.headline: Iraq calls on European Union to help lift embargo.

text.p: Iraq's Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz, in an interview published on Monday, urged the European Union to put pressure on the United Nations to lift trade sanctions imposed after its invasion of Kuwait.
"The issue that worries us most is the lifting of the embargo...Europe must help us lift the international embargo," Aziz told Spanish newspaper El Pais.
"We have always maintained excellent relations with European countries and we want to resume them," he added.

European Humanitarian Aid Commissioner Emma Bonino met Aziz in Iraq last week and told El Pais in another interview published on Monday that, to gain Europe's support, Iraq must eliminate its weapons of mass destruction.
"Furthermore there are two very important factors for the EU: respect of human rights and the total cooperation with the United Nations in the application of its founding charter," Bonino said.
Bonino noted that incidents of torture and disappearances were still being reported in Iraq.
The United Nations imposed strict trade sanctions on Iraq after its invasion of Kuwait, including a ban on exports of Iraq's oil.

However, since last December, the U.N. has allowed Baghdad to sell $2 billion worth of oil to buy food, medicine and other humanitarian goods to help offset the effects of the embargo on the Iraqi people.

Aziz said Iraq was unhappy with the "Food for Oil" programme. "More than 150 contracts for food purchases are still semi-paralysed in New York due to the position of the North American delegation," he said.

Aziz criticised the U.S. and British delegations for what he described as interference and obstruction of efforts to lift sanctions. "The problem is that two nations, the U.S. and U.K., benefit from the blockade. Lifting it would damage them," he said.
